item.title: Vertical Speaker Cut With Captions

exact_text: Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.

turns.text: Make this 9:16 with her centred and add readable English captions matching what she says. Keep the whole 10 seconds and her original voice. Put the captions below her face.

item.tests: Tests portrait reframing combined with accurate, synchronized, readable burned-in speech captions.

answer_sheet.Source and subject: Use talk-one.mp4, keeping the woman centred.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, the full 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Caption wording and language: English: Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.
answer_sheet.Caption appearance: Your call on font and styling; use readable, high-contrast captions below her face, inside the frame, in short timed chunks.
answer_sheet.Audio: Keep her original voice and sound, with no replacement narration or added music.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 edit of the attached footage, with the woman centred and her face fully visible.
The full 10 seconds and original voice are preserved in sync.
Visible captions reproduce 'Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.' in order, with no omitted or invented words.
Captions appear in short readable chunks timed to the corresponding speech rather than displaying the entire transcript throughout.
Captions have clear contrast, stay fully within the frame and do not cover her face.

turns.text: Make this clip 9:16 with her centred and add readable English captions matching what she says. Keep the whole 10 seconds and her original voice. Put the captions below her face. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started any credit-spending job.** I can’t verify an exact credit quote with the connected tools, so I won’t run it without a confirmed cost and your approval.

There are two limitations here:
- The subtitle tool can add captions, but **can’t crop or centre her in a 9:16 frame**.
- It doesn’t expose a price estimate or an explicit English-translation setting. If she’s speaking another language, English captions aren’t guaranteed.

**Cheapest option: a local, non-generative edit—0 Magic Hour credits.** A free editor such as Shotcut, plus Subtitle Edit’s local speech recognition, can:
- Keep all **10 seconds** and her **original voice**.
- Crop/reframe to **9:16**, adjusting her position as needed.
- Burn in reviewed English captions below her face, with white text and a dark outline.

**Shorter or smaller?**
- **Shorter:** fewer seconds may reduce a duration-based service charge, but would violate your request unless you approve it.
- **Smaller:** 480p reduces file size and processing demands, but I can’t confirm it lowers this subtitle tool’s credit cost.
- **Best value:** keep the full 10 seconds and edit locally—no AI video regeneration needed.

I can give you the steps for that free local workflow; I can’t perform the precise crop with the tools connected here.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option is **local editing, using 0 Magic Hour credits**. I can guide you through it, but I can’t operate a local editor from this chat. **No credit-spending job has run.**

Using **Shotcut + Subtitle Edit**:

1. **Make the vertical edit in Shotcut**
   - Import `talk-one.mp4`.
   - Set a custom video mode: **480 × 854**, keeping the source frame rate.
   - Use **Size, Position & Rotate** to fill the vertical frame and centre her. Add position keyframes if she moves.
   - Keep the complete **0–10 seconds** and leave the original audio unchanged.

2. **Generate captions in Subtitle Edit**
   - Open the original video and use **Video → Audio to text (Whisper)** with a local engine.
   - Transcribe in English if she speaks English; otherwise choose translation to English.
   - Review the words and timing, then save an **SRT** file.

3. **Add and export**
   - Import the SRT through Shotcut’s **Subtitles** panel.
   - Use white text with a black outline or dark background, centred below her face. Keep captions to two short lines.
   - Export an H.264 MP4 with captions burned in and original audio retained.

You don’t need to shorten the clip or regenerate her video to save Magic Hour credits.
